title: Ephemeral release channel for reproducible model packages and staged performance profile activation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create an ephemeral release channel pattern and CI automation that produces reproducible model packages, signs artifacts, and gates performance profile activation via staged canary channels. The goal is to reduce blast radius from onboarding errors, enable fast rollbacks, and centralize activation logic for performance profiles (runtime/quantization configs) separate from artifact publication.
background: Currently model onboarding CI publishes a single pinned artifact and immediately activates the associated performance profile. This conflates artifact publication with profile activation and makes rollbacks awkward. We want an ephemeral channel that holds signed, reproducible packages and a separate staged activation step for profiles so we can canary profiles independently from artifact rollout.
technical_design:
- CI produces hermetic tarball + manifest: gs://redwood-models/onboarded/<model>/<sha256>.tar.gz and a JSON manifest containing build metadata and deterministic file hashes.
- CI job 'ci/onboard/package-sign' creates an ephemeral channel record named ephemeral-releases/<timestamp>-<model>-<short-hash>. Channel TTL defaults to 7 days.
- Artifacts are cosign-signed using the onboard key stored in k8s secret 'cosign/onboard-key-v2' and uploaded to the artifact registry. The manifest includes cosign bundle reference.
- Profile activation is a separate CI step 'ci/onboard/activate-profile' which accepts a channel identifier and a canary policy. Activation writes a record to the profile-service with fields: channel, profile_id, rollout_policy. The profile-service will route traffic according to the canary policy and expose metrics for gating.
- Rollout policy supports percentages and time windows: example policy 5% for 2h, then 20% for 6h, then 100% if no regressions.
- We add a small shim in the model-resolver that can map pinned model references to ephemeral channels during canary windows, allowing consumers to opt-in to the channel via header or route flag.
- On success the ephemeral channel can be rotated into a permanent pin: pin-manifest <channel> -> registry pin <model>:vX.Y and TTL removed; this is a manual/automated promotion step controlled by release engineers.
acceptance_criteria: CI job builds hermetic package and uploads to artifact registry with deterministic manifest
Cosign signature and bundle are verifiable from the manifest using the onboard KMS key
Ephemeral channel record created and discoverable via API and Console (ephemeral-releases/<id>)
Profile activation can be triggered with a rollout policy and traffic is routed per policy
Ability to promote ephemeral channel to permanent pinned release via a single command
Rollback: deactivating the profile or deleting ephemeral channel immediately removes canary traffic
End-to-end integration test in ci/integration/onboard-ephemeral that simulates a canary and validates metrics gating
rollout_plan: 1) Merge CI jobs and manifest schema (staging). 2) Run weekly onboarding tests to produce ephemeral channels in staging for two model families. 3) Enable profile-service canary routing with header opt-in for 1 tenants. 4) Observe metrics for 48h. 5) Promote to permanent pin for one model; verify rollback path. 6) Graduate to production and update docs.
testing_plan: Unit tests for manifest generation and cosign verification, integration test exercising end-to-end build->sign->activate->route, chaos test that removes channel mid-rollout to validate graceful fallback to previous pinned model, and load test to ensure resolver has <5ms lookup overhead.
rollback_plan:
- Immediate: deactivate profile via profile-service API which moves traffic back to previous pin.
- If artifact proof is compromised: revoke cosign key and mark all ephemeral channels built with that key as quarantined; trigger re-sign pipeline.
- Promotion reversal: if promoted to pinned release, create a re-pin to previous commit and schedule a hotfix rollout.
security_considerations:
- Security review required for cosign key handling and TTL-based channels.
- Ensure manifests do not include secrets and that KMS usage is logged.
- Access controls: only release-engineers and CI bots may promote channels.
- Audit logs in console for channel create/activate/promote/delete actions.
open_questions: What default TTL should we use for ephemeral channels in production? (7d proposed)
Should promotion be fully automatic based on metric gates or require manual approval? (we propose manual by default, opt-in auto promote)
How do we surface ephemeral channels in Console without confusing users with permanent pins?
notes: Design reviewed with runtime and infra on 2026-03-05. Runtime team requested a lightweight resolver shim to avoid hot path DB reads; implemented a small in-memory cache with TTL. We also added a canary-exclusion list to avoid impacting high-sensitivity customers.
comments: 2026-03-01 Maya Chen: Initial proposal posted. Key idea: separate artifact publication from profile activation to reduce blast radius.
2026-03-05 Alex Rivera: Reviewed design with infra; agreed on cosign + KMS approach. Action: Alex to prototype resolver shim.
2026-03-07 Security (Priya Nambiar): Requested formal threat model for key usage and suggested HSM-backed signing if available. Marked ticket for security review.

2026-03-09 QA (Jordan Park): Integration test harness added to ci/integration; initial run produced expected routing but metrics gating flapped on noisy metric (latency p95). Added smoothing window to gating logic.
2026-03-12 Release Engineering (Lena Hofstad): Request to expose promote CLI for on-call; added exempt flag to skip auto-promote.

2026-03-14 Alex Rivera: Implemented package-sign job and ephemeral channel creation in staging. Next: wire activation step and add console surface. Blocked on console API rate-limit increase (ENG-74200).
decisions: Use cosign for signatures and store verification public keys in repo-managed trust anchors
Ephemeral channel default TTL = 7 days (can be overridden per-channel)
Promotion remains manual by default, with an opt-in auto-promote based on metric gates
Profile activation separated from artifact publish to allow independent canaries
next_steps: Add Console UI row for ephemeral channels and expose promote/deactivate actions
Complete security review and approve KMS/HSM plan
Run a staged canary for two low-traffic models in staging and collect gating metrics
